title: Steady Spine
intro: Two or three times a week, alongside your normal training. We walk first, then free up the hips and upper back, then build the brace that keeps the middle still, then unload. Nothing here stretches or rolls your lower back, because that is the one thing a sore back does not want.

before.label: Who it's for
before.text: Ordinary back pain that a doctor or physio has already looked at and cleared you to train through.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: Pain running down a leg, numbness, weakness in a leg or foot, or numbness between your legs. Also if your back pain started after a fall or a hit, or if it wakes you at night. If your bladder or bowel control changes, get seen the same day.

before.label: While you train
before.text: A bit of ache is fine. Sharp pain isn't, and neither is pain that builds through a set or feels worse the next morning. If it builds, stop that exercise. If it's sharp, stop the session.

exercises.name: Walk
exercises.note: An ache you can breathe through is fine, but if it turns sharp, stop that exercise and tell me.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.note: Wake the glutes up here and your back does less of their work for the rest of the session.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor with Overhead Reach
exercises.note: We free the hips and upper back so your lower back stops doing their job.

exercises.name: Modified Curl-Up
exercises.note: Leave this one for an hour after you wake up, when the discs are most swollen.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.note: Start on your knees and only move to the feet when the knee version is easy on both sides.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.note: Six reps, then four, then two, so it gets easier as you tire, and never to failure.

exercises.name: Supine Rest with Calves Elevated
exercises.note: No rolling and no back stretch here on purpose, because a sore back wants unloading, not pressure.

good: In through the nose for four, out for eight
Only the hand on your belly should move
